meanings.note: A woman who acts professionally; masculine acteur.

examples.text: Je ne suis pas actrice. Je veux juste voir Mathias.
examples.trans: I'm not an actress. I just want to see Mathias.

meanings.note: Understanding or surprise.
For liking things, places or activities.
For loving a person; adding bien often softens the sense to liking them.

examples.text: Tu n'aimais pas Mandelieu? C'est un bel endroit.
examples.trans: Didn't you like Mandelieu? It's a lovely place.

meanings.note: A sweetheart or boyfriend; feminine amoureuse.
As an adjective, amoureux de means in love with someone.

examples.text: Françoise avait un amoureux. Devine qui!
examples.trans: Françoise had a boyfriend. Guess who!

meanings.note: An author or creator; context can refer to a filmmaker.
For films shaped by a director's personal creative style.

examples.text: Line est devenue une star, et Françoise a fait du cinéma d'auteur.
examples.trans: Line became a star, and Françoise made art-house films.

meanings.note: Une autre = another (one).
Also a pronoun.

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

meanings.en: helper verb of the passé composé
meanings.note: J'ai appelé = I called.

meanings.en: il y a = there is, there are
meanings.note: Fixed expression.
À bientôt = see you soon.
as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...
as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...

meanings.en: bonne journée = have a nice day

meanings.note: Each one individually, taking a singular verb; feminine chacune.
A singer; masculine chanteur, feminine chanteuse.

examples.text: Line était une chanteuse connue. Françoise était une jeune actrice.
examples.trans: Line was a well-known singer. Françoise was a young actress.

meanings.note: Cinema as an art or industry, including acting in films.
A cinema building or movie theatre.

examples.trans: Shall we go to the cinema?

examples.text: Tu connais beaucoup de monde dans le cinéma. Tu pourrais m'aider.
examples.trans: You know lots of people in film. You could help me.

meanings.note: The past participle of connaître used descriptively: known or well-known.

examples.text: Line était une chanteuse connue. Françoise était une jeune actrice.
examples.trans: Line was a well-known singer. Françoise was a young actress.

meanings.note: Informal for daring or having a nerve; can be admiring or critical depending on tone.

examples.text: C'est culotté de la part de Gabriel.

meanings.note: D' before a vowel.
le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film
Also 'some': du sucre.

meanings.en: for (a length of time, still going on)
meanings.note: With an ongoing state, French normally uses the present: je suis ici depuis lundi.
A starting point: depuis lundi, since Monday.

examples.text: Je suis seule depuis trois mois.
examples.trans: I've been on my own for three months.

examples.text: Elle n'a pas travaillé depuis deux ans.
examples.trans: She hasn't worked for two years.

meanings.note: The x sounds like z before a vowel.
Become; uses être in the past, with agreement: elle est devenue.

examples.trans: He wants to become an actor.

examples.text: Line est devenue une star, et Françoise a fait du cinéma d'auteur.
examples.trans: Line became a star, and Françoise made art-house films.

meanings.note: Work out a guess; devine qui or devinez qui invites the listener to guess someone's identity.

examples.text: Françoise avait un amoureux. Devine qui!
examples.trans: Françoise had a boyfriend. Guess who!

meanings.note: Hate or strongly dislike; takes its object directly.

examples.text: J'en doute. Jean Gabin déteste les contrats.
examples.trans: I doubt it. Jean Gabin hates contracts.

meanings.note: for a feminine noun: l'industrie... elle
for a feminine noun: l'industrie... elle
For hearing sound, rather than deliberately listening.
In more formal contexts, can mean mean or understand.

examples.trans: I don't want to hear it!

examples.text: Ah bon? Je n'ai jamais entendu ça.

meanings.note: Can introduce two alternatives, places or people.

examples.text: Il n'y a rien entre nous.
S'il vous plaît. Il n'y a rien entre Mathias et moi, d'accord?
examples.trans: Please. There's nothing between Mathias and me, okay?

meanings.note: The t is never pronounced.
A standalone reply can mean exactly or that is right.

examples.text: Oui, exactement. Le Festival de Cannes.
examples.trans: Yes, exactly. The Cannes Film Festival.

meanings.note: for (duration): ça fait des mois que j'attends = I've been waiting for months

meanings.en: faire la surprise à = to surprise
ça fait trois semaines que = it's been three weeks since
meanings.note: With time.
A woman; the possessive context can distinguish this from wife.
Ma femme means my wife in a relationship context.

examples.text: Je ne sais pas. Tu es une femme, vous avez le même âge.
examples.trans: I don't know. You're a woman, you're the same age.

meanings.note: The bottom or back of something.
Figuratively, au fond means deep down or basically.

examples.trans: It's at the back on the right.

examples.text: Au fond, Françoise aurait aimé être chanteuse.
examples.trans: Deep down, Françoise would have liked to be a singer.

meanings.note: A story or account; histoire de introduces what it is about.
Also history as a field or past events.

examples.trans: It's the story of an old couple.

examples.text: C'est l'histoire d'un vieux couple qui fait des braquages.
examples.trans: It's the story of an old couple who do hold-ups.

meanings.note: Used with ne for never; in a compound past, follows the helper: je n'ai jamais vu.

examples.text: Je n'ai jamais vu un acteur aussi exigeant!
examples.trans: I have never seen such a demanding actor!

examples.text: Il ne répond jamais au téléphone pendant le week-end.
examples.trans: He never answers the phone during the weekend.

meanings.note: J' before a vowel.
Young; normally before the noun, and the singular spelling is the same for either gender.

examples.text: Je connais la ministre de la Culture. C'est une jeune femme brillante.
examples.trans: I know the Minister of Culture. She's a brilliant young woman.

meanings.note: A calendar day; tous les jours means every day.
Un jour can mean an unspecified day in the future.

examples.text: C'est facile, je sais. Mais je ne pensais pas faire ça un jour.
examples.trans: It's easy, I know. But I never thought I'd do it one day.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel
As a direct-object pronoun: le is masculine, la feminine; both become l’ before a vowel sound.
ne... pas = not; ne... rien = nothing; ne... que = only; n' before a vowel
parler à quelqu'un = to talk to someone
In à part, the combination means apart from or separately.

examples.text: Tout le monde est ici, à part lui.

meanings.note: second half of ne... pas; in speech ne is often dropped
With ne in a negative, no longer or no more.
In comparisons, more; plus tard means later and is pronounced without a final s sound.

examples.trans: I can't take any more, Andréa.

meanings.note: + infinitive.
conditional: tu pourrais, vous pourriez
Introduce one person to another; introduce the second person with à.
Can also mean formally presenting or offering something.

examples.text: Au nom de l'agence, je vous présente mes excuses.
examples.trans: On behalf of the agency, I apologise.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun.
Quelle surprise!.

examples.trans: How old would you say she is?

meanings.note: In qu’est-ce qui, the question expression supplies the subject, and need not refer to a person.

savoir.gloss: to know; to know how to

meanings.note: Je ne sais pas = I don't know.
+ infinitive: savoir monter.
Reflexive clitic used with third-person subjects; s’ before a suitable vowel sound.
Can describe perceiving a sensation or movement; se sentir describes how one feels.
Also used for smelling: ça sent bon, it smells good.

examples.text: J'ai senti un pied glisser vers la tombe.
examples.trans: I felt one foot slip towards the grave.

meanings.note: A celebrity; grammatically feminine even when the person is a man.

examples.text: Cette agence ne représente que des stars.

meanings.note: trouver quelqu'un sympa = to find someone nice

meanings.en: trouve quelque chose = think of something
meanings.note: In context.
one person you know well: friends, family, close colleagues
indefinite article; des in the plural
Number; l'un = one of them.
Vieil is used before a masculine noun beginning with a vowel sound; feminine vieille.

examples.text: Elle est trop vieille pour le rôle.
examples.trans: She's too old for the part.

examples.text: Trop vieille? C'est quoi le rôle, une gamine?
examples.trans: Too old? What's the part, a little girl?

meanings.note: Place: à Paris, à mon cours.
Time: à midi.

meanings.en: au = à + le, aux = à + les
meanings.note: Contractions.
Informal for cela.
With time.
The most common verb.
Ce + est.
